name: Geoteric: AI Seismic Interpretation for Energy
title: Geoteric: AI Seismic Interpretation for Energy
answer: Geoteric publishes software and services that apply deep learning and machine learning to seismic interpretation for oil, gas, geothermal and carbon storage work. Its site describes AI Faults networks, the Geoteric AI Hub for comparing networks, and Stratum for 3D fault detection, claiming fault interpretation time reductions of up to 95% and delivery of full-field AI fault interpretations in about two weeks.

sections.body: Geoteric is a seismic interpretation software company that says it has over thirty years of experience delivering subsurface technology to Energy companies and has completed more than 500 AI projects. Its website covers product pages for AI Faults 2D Networks, Geoteric AI Hub and Geoteric Stratum, an explainer on AI integration in seismic workflows, on-demand webinars, and case studies spanning oil and gas, offshore wind, carbon capture and storage, and geothermal-adjacent subsurface work.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The site explains AI as many technologies combined to let a machine act with human-like intelligence, with deep learning a subfield of machine learning and machine learning a subfield of AI. Supervised learning uses labelled data to recognise features in unseen data, unsupervised learning groups unlabelled data by similarity and variance, and self-organising maps are described as possibly the most common unsupervised method in subsurface understanding. Reinforcement learning is framed as a trial and error feedback loop. Applied to seismic, AI fault interpretations are described as full-field, from shallow overburden to reservoir, improving rigour for well planning. Geoteric AI Faults 2D Networks processes a data volume as 2D slices combined into a 3D fault volume, and interpreters can fine-tune networks with labels and fault sticks, with four to six lines usually enough to start. Geoteric Stratum detects faults in 3D using every data point and outputs a confidence cube with a traffic light fault probability display. The AI Hub lets geoscientists compare multiple networks and parameters in real time.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The site states AI fault interpretations can be provided in two weeks, that Geoteric AI has reduced seismic interpretation time from years to weeks, and that Stratum makes interpretation 90% faster. It says Geoteric is the first AI seismic interpretation provider to offer a choice of six trained and untrained neural networks, reducing fault interpretation time by up to 95%. The 2022.2 update added Acorn, an untrained network trainable on a user's own seismic data, and Meranti, a pre-trained network closer to traditional interpretation. Fine-tuning needs less than 0.03% of the seismic cube labelled, and in some projects faults interpreted numbered as low as 0.02%. AI Faults 2D Networks has been tested on volumes up to 350GB, with inlines or crosslines recommended not to exceed 12GB.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in Energy, this source shows how deep learning is being applied to a specific subsurface task, fault and horizon interpretation, and gives concrete adoption detail: network choices, fine-tuning thresholds, data size limits and claimed time savings. The case studies extend the same techniques beyond oil and gas to offshore wind site surveys, carbon capture and storage site screening, and shallow hazard assessment, which indicates where seismic AI is moving across the energy sector.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Energy

sections.body: The material is published by the vendor and is promotional in nature, so performance claims such as 95% time reduction and two-week delivery are not independently verified. Several pages are product descriptions or webinar listings rather than technical papers, and the case study page summarises projects without full methodology. The site gives no pricing, no independent benchmark and no detailed account of failure modes or accuracy limits.
